updates.name: Young shrub with toothed leaves (not stevia)
updates.note: Ethan: the stems are round (batch B4)

id_basis: Thin, woody brown stems with opposite pairs of light-green leaves that narrow to the base and are coarsely toothed toward the tip. It was taken for stevia, but the leaves have no sweetness at all (taste test, October 23), so it is not stevia. A square stem would point to the mint family (salvia); a round one to a hydrangea cutting or a eupatorium.

Thin, woody brown stems with opposite pairs of light-green leaves that narrow to the base and are coarsely toothed toward the tip. It was taken for stevia, but the leaves have no sweetness at all (taste test, October 23), so it is not stevia. The stems are round (Ethan, November 3), so it is not in the mint family (salvia and mint have square stems). That leaves a hydrangea cutting, a eupatorium or ageratina, or a chrysanthemum cutting.
